ai.title: Add OpenAI direct chat completions endpoint
ai.summary: Added `web/src/llm-api/openai.ts` to handle non-streaming chat completions directly via OpenAI API for supported models (currently `gpt-5`). Updated `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` to route requests to this new handler when `openai/gpt-5` is specified with non-streaming parameters, bypassing OpenRouter. Added `OPENAI_API_KEY` to `.env.example` and `packages/internal/src/env-schema.ts`. Renamed `reasoningModel` to `reasoningOptions` in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` for GPT-5 configuration.

eli5.text: The assistant can now talk directly to the newest GPT-5 model when you ask for multiple responses at once, skipping the usual middleman server that routes requests to different AI providers. If you look for it, you’ll notice a new settings field has been renamed to make GPT-5 think harder, and a placeholder for a new API key now sits alongside the existing ones. This is live today for any request that asks for GPT-5 and multiple answers, so you’d get a faster, more direct reply.

ai.title: Add n parameter to agent runtime for multi-response generation
ai.summary: Introduced `n` parameter in `PromptAiSdkFn` and `runAgentStep` to generate multiple responses. Refactored `editor-best-of-n` agents to use native `GENERATE_N` step type instead of spawning separate implementor agents. Updated `AgentStepContext` to return `nResponses` array. Affects `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, and `.agents/editor/best-of-n/`.

eli5.text: When you ask the writing assistant to come up with multiple versions of a solution, it can now do that directly in one go instead of spinning up a separate helper agent for each version. Behind the scenes, the assistant hands off the request to a built-in 'generate several' option, and all the different answers come back together in a single list for you to pick from. The old helper agents that used to handle this step have been removed, so the whole process is simpler and faster. You won't see two different agents running side by side anymore; you'll just get the batch of responses in one place.

ai.title: Revert random unit test fixes
ai.summary: Reverts commit titled "fix random unit tests failing". Restores user-agent runtime version to bun/1.2.23 in OpenRouter chat and completion test suites. Internal packages only.

eli5.text: The engineering team rolled back a previous patch that had temporarily adjusted two automated test files that verify how the app talks to OpenRouter’s chat and completion APIs. Only the tests were touched, the rollback restores the expected version stamp in those checks to bun/1.2.23 so the suite behaves consistently again, leaving all real product features unchanged. These are internal tests, so you won’t see or feel this while using the app.

ai.title: Add /feedback command and message feedback buttons to CLI
ai.summary: New /feedback slash command opens dedicated feedback input mode; each chat message now renders a feedback icon button. Feedback categories (good/bad/bug/other) with contextual placeholders and keyboard shortcuts (Escape cancel, Ctrl+C clear/cancel). Covers cli/src/components/feedback-*.tsx, chat.tsx, commands/router.ts, message-block.tsx. Feedback state isolated from main chat input; button hover triggers analytics event FEEDBACK_BUTTON_HOVERED.

eli5.text: The CLI now offers a /feedback command that opens a dedicated input area, and every message shows a feedback icon you can click to open that same area. You pick a category (good, bad, bug, or other), type your thoughts, and submit, with Escape cancelling and Ctrl+C clearing the entry; the feedback text is kept separate from the main chat input so typing does not shift or resize the chat box.

ai.title: Add --continue flag to restore last CLI chat state
ai.summary: New --continue CLI flag restores previous conversation context. Mechanism: run-state-storage.ts persists RunState and ChatMessage[] to disk; index.tsx parses flag; use-send-message.ts loads most recent state on mount, collapsing subagents/tools. Scope: CLI only (app.tsx, chat.tsx, project-files.ts). Detail: getMostRecentChatDir sorts chat directories by mtime; missing state logs 'No previous chat state found to continue from' without error.

eli5.text: You now have a new way to pick up a conversation where you left off in the command-line tool. Instead of starting a fresh chat every time you open the assistant, you can run it with a flag that reloads the most recent conversation, including the context and progress from before. If there's no prior chat to resume, it tells you that instead of crashing. This works today whenever you start the command-line tool with the new option.

ai.title: Add prompt and params to subagent events
ai.summary: printModeSubagentStartSchema and printModeSubagentFinishSchema in common/src/types/print-mode.ts now include optional prompt (string) and params (record) fields. executeSubagent in packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-utils.ts passes these fields into startEvent and finishEvent payloads. Scope: shared type definitions and agent runtime subagent spawn handler. Both fields are optional, preserving backward compatibility for existing event consumers.

eli5.text: When the system runs a smaller helper assistant inside the main one, it now sends along the exact instructions given to that helper and any settings chosen for it. If you watched the background activity log while a subassistant started up, you'd now see the prompt it was given and the options selected, making it easier to trace why that helper did what it did.

ai.title: CLI shows 'Generating n implementations' for editor-best-of-n
ai.summary: CLI now displays a status message 'Generating n implementations...' when running editor-best-of-n agents. This change propagates `params` and `prompt` from `subagent_start` events to `AgentContentBlock` in `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` and `cli/src/types/chat.ts`, allowing `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx` to render the count. The update affects CLI chat rendering, specifically within `AgentBranchWrapper`.

eli5.text: When you ask the CLI to generate multiple implementations of code using the editor-best-of-n mode, you'll now see a small status line like 'Generating 3 implementations...' appear in the chat, so you know it's working on the requested number. The change wires the count from the agent's settings through to the message display, adding it to the type definitions and propagating it from the start event to the rendering component, which then renders the text in a muted, italic style.

ai.title: Refactor CLI collapsed state to chat message metadata
ai.summary: Moved agent and block collapse state from separate Sets in `chat.tsx` to `isCollapsed` property on `ContentBlock` and `ChatMessage` metadata. Removed `collapsedAgents`, `autoCollapsedAgents`, `userOpenedAgents` props from `MessageBlock`, `ThinkingBlock`, `ToolBranch`, `AgentListBranch`. `handleCollapseToggle` now updates messages array directly. Scope: CLI chat components, hooks. Detail: Default collapse state changed to `true` for thinking blocks and agent lists, `false` for tool branches.

eli5.text: When you talk to the assistant in the CLI, things like thinking blocks and agent lists now start collapsed by default and remember whether you opened them, instead of the screen tracking all of that state separately behind the scenes. The app still stores that open/closed choice, but it does so right inside each message, which simplifies how the chat components work. You would notice that expanded sections stay open if you opened them, while everything else stays tucked away until you pull it up again.

ai.title: base2 max mode uses sonnet selector
ai.summary: base2 max mode now uses sonnet selector for editor-best-of-n. Removed gpt-5 from base2-max. Covers .agents/base2/base2.ts and .agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-best-of-n.ts. Deleted best-of-n-selector-gpt-5.ts and unified handleSteps to use sonnet selector only.

eli5.text: You can now get a smarter writing assistant. When your agent is set to its top-tier "max" mode, it now uses the same high-quality model (Claude's Sonnet) that the default editor uses, instead of a different model (GPT-5). This means the way it picks the best of several drafted edits is unified onto one proven system. You would notice it by watching the editor draft multiple solutions and then have one consistent reviewer choose the best one, rather than two different reviewers being used. The old, separate selector that used GPT-5 has been removed.
